name: s2
description: Ten MMLongBench-Doc samples: the three s0 samples (kept verbatim, same run ids) plus seven chosen for diversity. Covers all seven document types (research report, academic paper, guidebook, tutorial/workshop deck, financial report, brochure, administration file), every evidence source (pure text, layout text, table, chart, figure, cross-modal figure+text), two image-only documents that need OCR, every answer format (Str, Int, Float, List, None), single-page and multi-page evidence, two unanswerable questions (figure-side and text-side), and document lengths from 17 to 76 pages (287 pages in total). Each sample is one (doc_id, verbatim question) pair; run ids are stable so results are comparable with s0.
author: Muhammad Talal Majeed

samples.question: What is NARL stand for in this document?
samples.why_chosen: Born-digital text report (20 pages). Single-page pure-text evidence. Tests parser text extraction, index navigation and grounding on the easiest case.

samples.question: In Figure 1's demonstration, what are the color of the nodes that appear in all three clusters?
samples.why_chosen: Academic paper (23 pages). Requires inspecting Figure 1 as an image; the correct output is abstention (Not answerable). Tests the image tool and the verifier's abstention.

samples.question: Regarding the global iOS breakdown, what percentage of the pie chart was iOS 9?
samples.why_chosen: Slide deck with NO text layer (34 pages, image-only). Parser must OCR; index must locate the iOS breakdown slide; answer sits in a pie chart. Tests OCR, index and chart reading.

samples.question: What percentage of the shareholder was held by foreign companies and institutional investors as of March 31, 2007?
samples.why_chosen: Financial report (ITC Hotels annual report, 20 pages, born-digital text). Evidence is one shareholding TABLE on page 9; answer is a percentage (Float). Tests Docling table extraction, column lookup and numeric normalisation. The dataset asks the same question for 2017, which is unanswerable.

samples.question: How many Halls of Residence,  Residential colleges,  and student residences are there in NUS respectively? Please write the answer in list with ascending order, e.g., ["1","2"]
samples.why_chosen: Brochure (designed layout, 24 pages, 8 MB of graphics). Three counts spread over two pages (17-18) in layout-style text; answer is a List with a prescribed order. Tests multi-page aggregation, layout text and List formatting.

samples.question: How much time does it take from clifton campus to the city centre by bus? Your answer should be formatted as 'xx mins'.
samples.why_chosen: Guidebook, the longest document in the set (76 pages, heavy layout). One fact in a transport box near the end (page 61) with a mandated 'xx mins' format. Tests index navigation at scale, layout text and format compliance.

samples.question: Who produced the document that was revised on May 2018?
samples.why_chosen: Administration/Industry file (17 pages, born-digital text). A plausible-sounding text question (document producer, May 2018 revision) with no supporting evidence; gold is 'Not answerable'. Tests text-side abstention, complementing the figure-side abstention of run2.

samples.question: What's the percentage value of west Germany respondents viewing Germany's relationship with the United States is as important as its relationship with Russia?
samples.why_chosen: Research report (Pew, born-digital, 21 pages). Evidence is a bar CHART on page 15 whose labels are in the text layer; answer is a percentage (Float). Tests chart reading when Docling may capture the numbers as text, versus image inspection.

samples.question: How many reasoning steps are involved in the figure 1 in the paper?
samples.why_chosen: Academic paper (27 pages). Explicit 'figure 1' reference whose answer (a count, Int) IS in the figure on page 2, with supporting text. Counterpart of run2: the locator must resolve the caption and the vision model must count correctly instead of abstaining.

samples.question: In 2013, what is the total percentage of online adult users in the "White, Non-Hispanic" and "Hispanic" categories on the platform whose metrics include Followers, Tweet Clicks, Video Views, Tweet Reach, Engagement Rate, Completion Rate, Engagement: Mentions, Retweets, Likes, Top Tweet, Top Mention, Top Follower, Top Media Tweet, and Twitter Referral Traffic?
samples.why_chosen: Tutorial/Workshop slide deck with NO text layer (25 pages, image-only like run3). Multi-hop: identify the platform from its metrics list (page 18, figure) then add two percentages from a table (page 15); answer is an Int. Tests OCR, cross-page reasoning over Table+Figure evidence and arithmetic.
